text:
mira: quick flag - the edge starter's ESM build is collapsing our overloads to `any` for nodenext consumers. CJS is fine. anyone triaged this before?

dan: saw that. most likely a declaration resolution mismatch: ESM consumers expect an `index.mjs.d.ts` or follow the exports map, tsserver falls back to any if it can't find matching d.ts.

mira: here's a tiny repro: 
```ts
export function id(x: string): string;
export function id<T>(x: T): T;
export function id(x: any) { return x }
```
built to dist/esm/index.mjs + dist/cjs/index.cjs and a single dist/index.d.ts. editor shows id as (x: any) => any in Next/nodenext projects.

ryan: two fixes we use: 1) emit declarations to dist/types and copy index.d.ts to dist/esm/index.mjs.d.ts during postbuild; 2) or add a `typesVersions` mapping so TS chooses the right d.ts for ESM. both catch the lookup mismatch.

dan: also avoid using `any` in implementation if you care about overloads. change impl to `function id<T>(x: T): T { return x as T }` so the emitted d.ts preserves generics instead of widening.

mira: good call. adding a postbuild copy feels safest for the starter. tiny downside is added files in the package.

ryan: add a tsd test in CI that imports the built dist/esm entry and asserts the overload/generic shape — that will surface regressions automatically.

ci-bot: created issue #511: "starter: ESM consumers see collapsed overloads / any" and branch starter/511-fix-esm-types.

dan: sounds like a plan. mira, want help with the PR? I can add the tsd workflow snippet.

mira: yes please. i'll include a README blurb about nodenext vs bundler resolution and link to a short repro. will ping eng-devex for review once ready.

ryan: one more note: recommend `moduleResolution: bundler` for contributor dev setups to match Vite/Next behavior, but CI should run `tsc` with `moduleResolution: node` to verify publish artifacts.

mira: thanks all — i'll open PR now and link it here.
